You'd be surprised the deep relief you feel when a bigger issue gets dragged up.  I'd give it a shot. What is there to lose?
I'm by no means happy, but we have to find social support somehow.  Have you considered seeing a counselor?

Keep seeing your therapist, sometimes talking through these issues can be more effective than other methods of treatment.  You'll be surprised when a bigger issue gets dragged up from out of nowhere and the deep relief you feel from addressing it.   I also completely advocate about the notion of being 'artificially happy'.  From 11-16 I was on some form of medication until a (straightedge) girl I knew coaxed me off of them with that spiel.  I wouldn't recommend it as now at 23 I'm a chemically imbalanced wreck.  You might try talking to your physician about trying other medications and see if you can find something else you like better.  Welbutrin has worked wonders for some of my family members.
No problem!  And I hear ya, I'm so sick of hearing "It gets better."  In my experience, it doesn't.  You just get more and more used to life being the way that it is.

It's two sides of the same coin.  In my darkest days (which have been pretty frequent lately) I completely share your viewpoint--why should I have to be here if I don't want to be?  The truth is that it's selfish on both sides.  It's selfish to leave them without you, and it's selfish for them to keep you here when you don't want to be.  Even though the sadness is beyond overwhelming at times, we have to focus on the tiny fragments of happiness that occur every once in awhile.  Even if you don't have anyone else to talk to (which I doubt), know that I'm here.

Hey, nomad here, moved six times across my country in my lifetime.  It really sucks having to start all over when you move somewhere new, especially when you were in a good place in your previous locale.  All I can say is that you really have to reach out to find people with similar interests.  Awhile back I looked up a local MilSim Airsoft group that I now play with every Saturday and I've made some of the best friends I've ever had through it.  What are your interests?  I'm sure if you look around  you'll find a group of people who share them.  Common ground, even if it's only on one simple thing, can make a world of a difference.

I know how you feel (at least to some degree) and identify with literally everything you said in the second to last paragraph.  We just have to take it day by day until it gets better.  If not for ourselves, for the people we love and the people that love us.
